April 30, 2016
Michelle Roberts
Chief Financial Officer
Dyer and Sons
Dear Ms. Roberts,
Thank you for asking us to review the property before Dyer and Sons commits to the
purchase. This letter sets out the terms on which we will carry out a Phase I
Environmental Site Assessment for Dyer and Sons, and it records in writing what we
discussed by telephone last week. I have kept it plain, because you should know
exactly what you are engaging us to do before any work begins. Please read it
through, and if any part of it differs from what you expected, call me and we will
settle it before you sign.
The Assessment We Will Carry Out
A Phase I assessment is a review of a property's environmental history and its
present condition. We conduct it to the current ASTM standard, E1527-13, which is
the practice a lender or a buyer will expect us to have followed. The purpose is to
identify recognized environmental conditions, the term of art for evidence that a
release of a hazardous substance has occurred, is occurring, or is likely to have
occurred on the property. Where we find such evidence we will say so, and where
we do not, we will say that as well.
The work falls into a records review, a site visit, and a set of interviews, and the
report draws the three together. We examine historical aerial photographs, fire-
insurance maps, chain-of-title material, and any prior environmental reports on the
property. We commission a regulatory database search covering the parcel and the
sites around it, and we read what the federal and state records show about the
property and its neighbors. One of our scientists then walks the site and
photographs what is there, and we speak with people who know its history. None of
this involves sampling soil or groundwater. A Phase I is a paper-and-observation
study, and if it turns up a condition that warrants testing, that testing is a separate
piece of work we would scope with you at the time.

Who Will Do the Work
I will oversee the engagement and sign the report that reaches you, and I read every
report before it leaves this office. James Henderson, one of our environmental
scientists, will lead the records review and the regulatory research and will write
the assessment; the desk work behind a Phase I is his particular strength. Mary
Foster, our field technician, will conduct the site reconnaissance and keep the
photographic record. John Sanchez, our senior scientist, will review the findings
before I do, and he will tell me plainly if the record does not support a conclusion.
Between us you have the whole of the firm's technical bench on this file.
Fee and Schedule
We will carry out the assessment for a fixed fee of $34,000, which covers the
records review, the regulatory database search, the site visit, the interviews, and the
written report. The fee does not move with the findings, so you know the cost of the
work at the outset. We are ready to begin on May 10, 2016, and we expect to have
the report to you approximately four months after we start, allowing for the
turnaround of the regulatory database search and the records we request from third
parties. If anything in the file threatens that timing, you will hear it from me early,
not at the end.
Fees and Payment
We invoice the fixed fee in two parts: half on your signing of this letter, and the
balance on delivery of the report. Invoices are payable within thirty days of the date
they carry. Any direct costs we arrange on your behalf, such as the regulatory
database subscription or the retrieval of archived records, are included in the fixed
fee and are not billed separately, so there is nothing unexpected on a later
statement.
Term and Termination
The engagement begins when you sign this letter and ends when we deliver the
report and you have paid for it. Either of us may end it earlier on written notice. If
you end it before we finish, we will bill you for the work completed to that point and
hand over what we have produced. If we end it, which we would do only for a reason
we could explain to you, we will not bill for work left undone.
Confidentiality
We treat what we learn about the property and about Dyer and Sons as yours, and
we do not discuss your business with anyone outside the engagement without your

consent. The report is prepared for your use and for the lender or counsel you name
to us. We keep our working file for the period our professional standards require,
and we release it to no one else without your instruction or a lawful demand we
cannot refuse.
Limitation of Liability
A Phase I assessment reduces uncertainty; it does not remove it. It reflects the
records that exist and are reasonably ascertainable, the condition of the property on
the day we see it, and the recollections of the people we interview, and it cannot
account for what those sources do not disclose. For that reason our liability arising
out of this engagement is limited to the amount of the fee, except where the law
does not permit such a limit. This is the ordinary term for work of this kind, and I
am glad to talk it through if it gives you pause.
Governing Law
This agreement is governed by the law of the state in which the property lies, and
any dispute under it will be resolved in the courts of that state. We would of course
try to settle any disagreement between us directly before it reached that point.
If these terms match your understanding, please sign both copies of this letter and
return one to me, and we will begin the assessment on the date named above. I am
glad to be working with you on this, and please feel free to call me directly at any
point while the work is underway.
Angela Flynn
Managing Principal
Date: April 30, 2016
Michelle Roberts
Chief Financial Officer, Dyer and Sons
